comparison: Strong agreement on core behavioral findings (C1-C3, C11-C18, C21, C24, C63, C71). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing and well-supported. Peer review also includes C19-C20 and C22-C23 in this grouping, while OpenEval evaluates these separately (R7, R8). Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on neuronal manipulation experiments (C51-C55). Both evaluations find the activation/inhibition data convincing with appropriate controls. Both rate as SUPPORTED with no concerns raised.

Significant disagreement on receptor localization claims (C56-C62). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the anatomical and functional evidence convincing. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 raising a critical concern about Figure 6E appearing to contradict the proposed model where receptor knockdown restores rather than reduces activity.

Strong agreement on dopamine necessity (C25-C35). Both evaluations find the pharmacological, genetic, and optogenetic evidence convincing. Peer review groups these with broader dopamine claims (C4, C10, C76-C78) while OpenEval separates circuit anatomy (R2) from necessity experiments (R3). Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on receptor specificity findings (C44-C50, C47, C95). Both evaluations accept the differential receptor requirements (Dop1R1/Dop2R vs DopEcR). Peer review frames this as an 'intriguing discrepancy' requiring further investigation but still finds the data convincing. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on neural circuit connectivity (C37-C43). Both evaluations praise the multi-method approach including calcium imaging, GRASP, and optogenetics. Peer review emphasizes the 'state-of-the-art methods' while OpenEval highlights the convergence of independent techniques. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on differential receptor requirements (C47, C48, C95) distinguishing sexual failure from starvation pathways. OpenEval notes C48's mechanistic interpretation is speculative but rates SUPPORTED. Peer review presents this as a valuable contribution highlighting circuit specificity, also rating SUPPORTED.

Agreement on cVA control experiment (C19-C20). OpenEval evaluates this separately as effectively ruling out cVA, rating SUPPORTED. Peer review includes these claims within the broader behavioral findings (R1) without specific concerns.

Agreement on Satisfied-Failed male experiment (C22-C23). OpenEval evaluates this separately, finding it demonstrates the effect is actively induced by failure experience, rating SUPPORTED. Peer review includes these claims within the broader behavioral findings without specific concerns.

Partial agreement on dopamine reward interpretation (C73-C79). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C74 and C79 are speculative beyond the data. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing the novelty of cross-behavioral integration while appropriately framing speculative aspects as discussion points.

Agreement on evolutionary significance speculation (C97-C99). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable speculations without supporting data. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED but frames these appropriately as discussion points about future research directions.

Agreement on cross-behavioral effects and novelty (C65-C66, C72). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes C72's common mechanism suggestion is speculative. Peer review emphasizes the valuable contribution of showing mating failure modulates feeding, rating SUPPORTED.

Agreement on contextual literature claims (C6-C9). OpenEval finds these well-established principles properly cited, rating SUPPORTED. Peer review accepts the contextual framing without concerns, noting literature was appropriately updated.

Partial overlap on emotion-like state interpretation (C83). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the connection to emotions is plausible but not directly demonstrated. Peer review includes this within broader novelty claims (R7) rated as SUPPORTED, framing it as adding a new dimension to understanding.

Agreement on emotion literature context (C80-C82). OpenEval rates the overall interpretation as UNCERTAIN due to speculative aspects. Peer review accepts the contextual framing (C80-C82) without specific concerns as part of background literature.

Agreement on consumption volume finding (C86). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting the effect is on initiation threshold rather than consumption. Peer review includes this methodological detail within accepted contextual claims without concerns.
Agreement on mating failure literature context (C64, C68-C70). OpenEval finds these accurately cite prior literature, rating SUPPORTED. Peer review accepts these contextual claims without concerns.

Agreement on dopamine reward literature (C76-C78). OpenEval includes these as accurately cited prior work but rates overall interpretation as UNCERTAIN due to speculative aspects. Peer review includes these within dopamine findings rated as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on circuit claims (C4, C10, C35). OpenEval groups these with detailed circuit connectivity evidence (C37-C43) rating SUPPORTED. Peer review groups these with dopamine necessity experiments, also rating SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on C71. OpenEval includes this in literature context about extending knowledge to feeding, rating SUPPORTED. Peer review includes it within core behavioral findings, also rating SUPPORTED.
